description: >-
  The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution dataset for clinical
  care AI. It is produced by the CHoRUS project, described by the project site as one
  data generation project of four in the National Institute of Health (NIH) funded
  Bridge2AI consortium, and as the collection of multi-modal data across 14 different
  hospitals that uses ongoing and new standardization practices. Data collection is
  retrospective and access is controlled. The September 2025 AIM-AHEAD informational
  webinar states that, as of August 2025, the dataset covers 14 different hospitals with
  over 45K unique admissions. The CHoRUS project site's "Current Released Dataset"
  snapshot lists 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU, 1.6 billion rows of
  EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data. The
  data types named in the webinar's CHoRUS dataset table are demographics; medication
  administration (dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration);
  procedures (documentation by providers); nursing flowsheets (high-frequency
  documentation); diagnoses (documentation by providers); clinical notes (extracted and
  tokenized using OHNLP toolkit); imaging (from PACS); waveform telemetry (bedside
  monitors, gateway/middleware); and waveform EEG (hospital database). The same webinar
  states that OMOP and telemetry are in the enclave except that clinical notes are stored
  locally except tokens, that imaging currently has 1000 images available with
  de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and that EEG extraction is in process
  at this point.
conforms_to: >-
  The CHoRUS dataset table presented in the September 2025 informational webinar names the
  following data standards for the dataset's data types: OMOP, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, and
  EDF+ and Persyst. The row label for clinical notes itself states that they are extracted
  and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit. The NIH RePORTER project abstract states, as a
  project plan, that the project will standardize data to the OMOP Common Data Model, and
  the CHoRUS project site reports 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data in its current
  released dataset. The published metadata schemas named in the same table are the OMOP
  schema, the OMOP schema with extensions, the OHNLP open source schema, the DICOM schema,
  the PhysioNet schema extended, and the open source EDF+ and Persyst schema.

  - grant_number: OT2OD032701
  notes: >-
    The CHoRUS project site states that the project is funded by the NIH under award number
    OT2OD032701. The NIH RePORTER record for this award lists application ID 10472824,
    project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, title "Bridge2AI:
    Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for
    Equitable AI", principal investigator ROSENTHAL, ERIC S., organization MASSACHUSETTS
    GENERAL HOSPITAL, fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and
    project end 2026-11-30.
purposes:
- response: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states, as a project plan, that the CHoRUS data
    generation project will meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at
    characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring
    treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states as the project's overarching goal that it will
    develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset, while ensuring the methods
    promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, while promoting a new generation
    of AI clinicians and scientists.
- response: >-
    The CHoRUS project site states that the goal is to work with projects to create
    ethically sourced datasets and tools around Artificial Intelligence and to create best
    practices for AI in health.
- response: >-
    The CHoRUS GitHub organization overview (historical documentation captured 2025-11-14)
    states as a goal that the CHoRUS Network is to develop the most diverse,
    high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the grand challenge of
    improving recovery from acute illness.
tasks:
- response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
- response: Predicting complications.
- response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states that there is an urgent need for infrastructure
    to support artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) in critical care, and
    that developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first step towards
    actionable and trustworthy AI.

- split_details: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states, as a project plan, that the dataset will also
    provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation to aid
    marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical
    care.
acquisition_methods:
- acquisition_details: >-
    Retrospective data collection, as stated in the September 2025 CHoRUS informational
    webinar.
raw_data_sources:
- source_description: Imaging obtained from PACS.
- source_description: Waveform telemetry obtained from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware.
- source_description: Waveform EEG obtained from a hospital database.
sampling_strategies:
- strategies: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states, as a project plan, that the project will
    establish a legal framework for collecting data at scale, sampling to ensure
    comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies.
- strategies: >-
    The CHoRUS GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) states, as a future
    capability, that federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and
    diverse cohort.
preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Standardization of electronic health record data to the OMOP Common Data Model. The
    CHoRUS project site reports 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data in its current released
    dataset, and the NIH RePORTER project abstract states as a project plan that the project
    will standardize data to the OMOP Common Data Model.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit, as stated in the
    CHoRUS dataset table of the September 2025 informational webinar.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    EEG extraction was in process at the time of the September 2025 informational webinar.
labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    The CHoRUS GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) states, as a future
    capability, that a visualization and annotation environment will label data with targets
    important for prediction. The NIH RePORTER project abstract likewise states, as a project
    plan, that the project will develop capabilities across a multi-center network to
    acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize, and label data.
is_deidentified:
  deidentification_details: >-
    The September 2025 informational webinar states that imaging currently has 1000 images
    available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and that clinical notes
    are stored locally except tokens. The NIH RePORTER project abstract states, as a project
    plan, that the project will transform data using approaches that limit re-identification.
license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    All participants must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form
    before gaining access to the dataset, as stated for Cohort 2 of the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI
    for Clinical Care Training Program in the September 2025 informational webinar.
data_governance:
  access_review_process: >-
    Access to the dataset is controlled. For Cohort 2 of the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for
    Clinical Care Training Program, participants fill out a registration form with name,
    email, and institution, and once access is granted and compute is provisioned an email
    will be sent; a ".edu" email address is needed in order to gain access to the dataset,
    and program administrators will assist with this access if needed. The CHoRUS GitHub
    organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) directs access requests to dbold@emory.edu
    or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org.
regulatory_restrictions:
  confidentiality_level: restricted
intended_uses:
- use_category: AI/ML model development for acute and critical care
  usage_notes: >-
    The NIH RePORTER project abstract states that CHoRUS will develop the necessary network,
    tools, standards, data, and education to build machine-learning (ML) and artificial
    intelligence (AI)-derived models to improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring
    critical care.
- use_category: Hands-on AI/ML training
  usage_notes: >-
    The AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program expands access to Bridge2AI
    CHoRUS data through engagement, AI training, and mentorship; trainees receive hands-on
    training on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Network and leverage the data and
    tools to create practical use cases.
- use_category: Downstream analytics on the mapped and assembled dataset
  usage_notes: >-
    The CHoRUS GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) invites those interested
    in getting involved in downstream analytics on the mapped and assembled dataset to reach
    out using its contact details.
existing_uses:
- examples:
  - Datasets are being used for training activities (September 2025 CHoRUS informational webinar).
- examples:
  - Datasets are being used for publications (September 2025 CHoRUS informational webinar).
updates:
  update_details: >-
    The CHoRUS project site's "Anticipated Final Dataset" snapshot gives 100,000 patient
    admissions, 9 different data modalities, 14 data contributing hospitals, and 60+ CHoRUS
    consortium members across 20 different institutions. The September 2025 informational
    webinar states that de-identification was in process for a larger imaging cohort and
    that EEG extraction was in process at that point, and its CHoRUS dataset table records
    "Planned" for some entries in its metadata column.
extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai#table-of-contents
  extension_details: >-
    The CHoRUS GitHub organization overview (captured 2025-11-14) describes how contributors
    take part. For data managers at data contributing sites, the starting reference is the
    Chorus_SOP page, which holds an interactive workflow diagram describing the step-by-step
    process for extracting and contributing clinical data to CHoRUS, with dynamic links to
    SOP documents that have undergone internal validation and review within the Chorus_SOP
    repository, and issues can be posted in the Standards or Data Acquisition discussion
    locations. For clinical collaborators, a chorus-mapping repository has been established
    with documentation and pooled tabular mappings along with an associated clinical
    validation SOP for contributing to mapping efforts. Data contributing sites have been
    asked to provide regular status updates on their progress in creating and curating a
    CHoRUS-specific clinical data extract, submitted either through the GitHub interface or
    by a Google Form.
external_resources:
- external_resources:
  - >-
    CHoRUS GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai#table-of-contents), which
    houses active repositories providing software and tooling to interact with and extract
    insight from clinical data in diverse formats, validated semantic mappings, standard
    operating protocols for data contributing sites, and project management overviews.
- external_resources:
  - >-
    Website listed in the CHoRUS GitHub organization overview contact section:
    www.bridge2ai.org/chorus
notes: >-
  The CHoRUS project website carries the notice "This repoitory is under review for
  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives." (spelling as
  published). The project site organizes CHoRUS into the components Data, Ethics and
  People: under Ethics it states that the consortium evaluates community perspectives on
  clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in
  AI, and that new approaches are being created as the existing legal and regulatory
  landscape is analyzed; under People it states that the project is dedicated to training
  engineers, data scientists, and clinicians. The NIH RePORTER project abstract describes
  the same structure as three pillars: 1) Data (Standards, Tool Development and
  Optimization, and Data Acquistion) 2) Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI) and 3) People
  (Team Science and Skill and Workforce Development).
source_caveats: >-
  Table structure: the CHoRUS dataset table in the September 2025 informational webinar was
  extracted from slide text with its columns (Data type, Data standard, Access control,
  Metadata, Published metadata schema) separated from their rows, so this record names the
  data types, standards, access markings and published metadata schemas the table contains
  without asserting which cell belongs to which row, except where a row label itself names
  the standard, as in "Clinical notes (extracted and tokenized using OHNLP toolkit)".
  Counts: the project site (documentation, the highest-ranked source in this bundle)
  separates an "Anticipated Final Dataset" snapshot (100,000 patient admissions, 9 different
  data modalities, 14 data contributing hospitals, 60+ consortium members across 20
  different institutions) from a "Current Released Dataset" snapshot (50,000 patient
  admissions, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, 23 Tb
  waveform data); only the current-released figures are recorded here as present data, and
  the anticipated figures are carried as anticipated. The webinar's "over 45K unique
  admissions" is dated to August 2025 and is a lower bound, so it is compatible with the
  site's 50,000 figure rather than in conflict with it, and both are retained. License: the
  only license statement in the bundle is the CHoRUS GitHub organization README's "This
  project is licensed under the MIT License", which concerns that GitHub project and its
  repositories; no license is stated for the dataset itself, so the license slot is left
  empty. Identifier: no dataset DOI appears in any source document, so the project site URL
  is used as this record's identifier. The GitHub organization overview is historical
  documentation captured 2025-11-14.

Abstract Text
There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) in critical care. Developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first step towards actionable and trustworthy AI. As part of the NIH Common Fund’s Bridge2AI program, the CPatient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Clinical Care AI data generation project will meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness. Through 3 pillars, the CHoRUS data generation project will addresses multiple challenges relevant for acquiring an AI-ready data set from more than 100,000 critically ill patients: 1) Data (Standards, Tool Development and Optimization, and Data Acquistion) 2) Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI) and 3) People (Team Science and Skill and Workforce Development). The project’s overarching goal is to develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset, while ensuring the methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, while promoting a new generation of AI clinicians and scientists. The dataset will also provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care. Drawing expertise from a comprehensive set of disciplines such as team science, law, ethics, health services, biomedical science, engineering, and scientific journal publications, this project will A) establish a legal framework for collecting data at scale, sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies; B) perform community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing; C) ensure that data elements feature appropriate contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital; D) develop capabilities across a multi-center network to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize, and label data such as structured electronic health record data, tokenized unstructured electronic health record data, telemetry and EEG waveforms, imaging, and social determinants of health; E) acquire data, standardize data to the OMOP Common Data Model, transform data using approaches that limit re-identification, and label data for ; and F) cultivate expertise in the lay and scientific community to improve AI literacy nd utilization through multimodal educational approaches. To accomplish this, the project will involve extensive collaboration between centers as well as through the NIH Bridge2AI program, the NIH Bridge2AI Bridge Center, external biomedical and clinical organizations, industry, and regulatory agencies.

The Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI will develop the necessary network, tools, standards, data, and education to build machine-learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived models to improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring critical care.  By performing legal and ethical research, developing tools for data storage, labeling and analysis, acquiring and standardizing a dataset of unprecedented diversity and high resolution, sequestering holdout datasets for external validation, and enriching the community through education, this data generation project will catalyze the biomedical research and expertise necessary to promote the patient-focused deployment of AI in acute and critical care.

About

CHoRUS for Equitable AI

The goal of the CHoRUS Network is to develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically

sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute

illness.

This collaboration spans 20 academic centers, of which 14 will contribute as Data

Acquisition centers.

Patient-focused efforts will determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy

and bias, while accounting for Social Determinants of Health.

Unified standards will harmonize multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data.

A visualization and annotation environment will label data with targets important for

prediction.

A comprehensive set of approaches will develop the skills and workforce for a next

generation of diverse academic and community AI scientists.

Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort.

Collaborating with Bridge2AI and 3 other data generation projects, the CHoRUS Network will

help us cross the Bridge2AI network together.

Get Started

The CHoRUS GitHub organization houses active repositories that provide:

1. Software and tooling to interact with and extract insight from clinical data in diverse

formats

2. Validated semantic mappings for connecting clinical data in various source formats to

international standards

3. Standard operating protocols (SOPs) to instruct data contributing sites about best

practices for curating and delivering interoperable datasets

4. Project management overviews to help track data delivery statuses and complex task

dependencies within CHoRUS

We've defined different groups of anticipated users of this GitHub in the sections below, and

direct those users to appropriate locations within the chorus-ai repository space.

(back to top)

The starting reference for data managers at data contributing sites is the Chorus_SOP page.

Here, you will find an interactive workflow diagram describing the step-by-step process for

extracting and contributing clinical data to CHoRUS, with dynamic links to various SOP

documents that have undergone an internal validation and review process within the

Chorus_SOP repository.

Project Managers

We've established two different modes of project management within the chorus-ai
organization:

1. Task tracking among CHoRUS members and across teams

2. Status tracking of data contributing sites to identify and resolve any blocking issues

Task Tracking

We are aggregating issues across various repositories into an overall task management

project. In this GitHub project, we assign users to tasks, create and track anticipated

delivery dates, and highlight dependencies between tasks and users. Several per-repo
projects are also active, but we are in the process of phasing those projects out and

migrating their contents to this central project space.

Status Tracking

We have asked data contributing sites to provide regular status updates with regard to their

progress in creating and curating a CHoRUS-specific clinical data extract. Sites can submit

updates either using the GitHub interface directly, or by submitting a Google Form (please

reach out to get a link to the form if you'd like to submit an update for your site). We've

created a GoogleScript that is triggered on each Google Form submission and makes calls
to the GitHub API to update status and issue information appropriately. These site statuses

end up in either the Standards Project or the Data Acquisition Project.
